summary: @ornikar/eslint-config-formatjs preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares preinstall=`node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style renaming (identifiers such as `_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`) and string-property indirection, and downloads a Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts the `bun` binary, chmods it +x, and then invokes `execFileSync(bun, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')])`. The sibling `math_init.js` is a 727 KB Bun-compiled bundle (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`) containing a large hex string array and rotation function so it is unreadable to Node and only executable under the dropped Bun runtime. The package's advertised purpose is an ESLint formatjs config, which has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime or execute an opaque compiled bundle at install time. This matches the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: the runtime is legitimate (oven-sh/bun) but is fetched solely to run attacker-shipped, obfuscated code on the installer's host on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
